output.headline: Accepts a $390,000 grant from county Probation for high school-to-middle school mentoring
output.summary: The district is signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the Alameda County Probation Department and accepting a $390,000 grant. It funds the Cross-Age Mentoring Program, where high school students mentor middle school students one-on-one, at Oakland High, Westlake Middle and Roosevelt Middle schools. The term is June 1, 2019 to September 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts a $382,623.42 donation from Chabot Elementary PTA for staff salaries and hardware
output.summary: The district is accepting a $382,623.42 donation from the Anthony Chabot Elementary School PTA for Chabot Elementary School. The money supplements staff salaries and pays for hardware at the school during the 2019-20 school year.

output.headline: Accepts a $135,402 PTA donation to fund three recess coach positions at Montclair Elementary
output.summary: The district is signing a fiduciary agreement with the Montclair Elementary School PTA and accepting a $135,402 donation. The money pays for three full-time enrichment recess coach positions at Montclair Elementary School during the 2019-20 school year.

output.headline: Ratifies BLX Group's up-to-$5,000 review of the district's bond disclosure compliance

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The Board ratifies a contract with BLX Group LLC of Los Angeles to review five years of the district's required continuing disclosures on its outstanding bonds and write a report of its findings. Payment is capped at $5,000. The work period began June 20, 2019, before this approval, and runs through August 31, 2019.

output.headline: Ratifies $1.96M in gifts, grants and bequests the district accepted in 2018-19
output.summary: The Board is formally approving the annual report of gifts, grants and bequests the district accepted during the 2018-19 fiscal year. The cumulative total is $1,963,627.06, with the individual gifts listed in an exhibit to the report.

output.headline: Ratifies $15.67M in June 2019 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, payroll payments made from June 1 through June 30, 2019: 896 printed payroll checks and 7,090 direct deposits. The cumulative amount is $15,670,422.57.

output.headline: Ratifies $13.35M in July 2019 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, payroll payments made from July 1 through July 31, 2019: 3,406 printed payroll checks and 4,965 direct deposits. The cumulative amount is $13,353,446.37.

output.headline: Ratifies $45.82M in accounts payable checks issued in June 2019
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, 1,661 accounts payable checks the district printed from June 1 through June 30, 2019 to pay its bills. The cumulative amount is $45,822,224.24.

output.headline: Ratifies $19.64M in accounts payable checks issued in July 2019
output.summary: The Board is approving, after the fact, 648 accounts payable checks the district printed from July 1 through July 31, 2019 to pay its bills. The cumulative amount is $19,637,630.48.

output.headline: Updates who may sign for 10 district financial accounts
output.summary: The Board is adopting ten resolutions (Nos. 1920-0007 through 1920-0016) naming the authorized signers on district financial accounts. The accounts include the cafeteria account, the revolving fund, payroll accounts, the workers' compensation account and investment accounts. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Adopts state fiscal team's student body accounting manual and fraud prevention guide
output.summary: The Board is adopting a manual from the Fiscal Crisis & Management Assistance Team (FCMAT), a state-supported team that helps districts with finances. It covers how to account for Associated Student Body (ASB) money, such as student club and activity funds, and how to prevent fraud. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Accepts $250,000 from the City of Oakland for academic support at four high schools
output.summary: The district is accepting a $250,000 grant from the City of Oakland, through the Oakland Fund for Children and Youth. It pays for academic support and case management in the African American Male Achievement and Oakland Athletic League programs at Castlemont, Fremont, McClymonds and Skyline High Schools, from July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $50,000 from Salesforce Foundation for Middle School Network communications
output.summary: The district is accepting $50,000 from the Salesforce Foundation, paid through the Oakland Public Education Fund as fiscal agent. The money supports marketing and communication for the Middle School Network, aimed at increasing funding and teacher retention, from April 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $12.18M from the state for the California State Preschool Program in 2019-20
output.summary: The district is accepting a $12,175,510 grant award from the California Department of Education for the California State Preschool Program, run by the district's Early Childhood Education Department. The contract covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $7,500 from the state for the Pre-Kindergarten and Family Literacy Program
output.summary: The district is accepting a $7,500 grant award from the California Department of Education for the Pre-Kindergarten and Family Literacy Program, run by the district's Early Childhood Education Department. The contract covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $2.59M from the state for general child care and development programs
output.summary: The district is accepting a $2,586,937 grant award from the California Department of Education for the state's General Child Care and Development Program, run by the district's Early Childhood Education Department. The contract covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $170,280 to Ninyo & Moore's Fremont High construction contract for vapor well work
output.summary: This amendment adds $170,280 to the district's contract with Ninyo & Moore, raising the limit from $226,237 to $396,517. The firm will prepare a technical memo for the California Department of Toxic Substances Control and handle added work on installing, sampling and destroying vapor wells for the Fremont High School new construction project.

output.headline: Pays SunPower up to $95,755.20 to replace the solar array at Oakland Technical High
output.summary: The district is hiring SunPower Corporation to remove and replace the solar array at Oakland Technical High School. Work runs from August 15, 2019 to no later than October 31, 2019, for no more than $95,755.20.

output.headline: Adds $80,000 and extends Anthonio's inspector services for the Foster the Center project to May 2020
output.summary: This amendment adds $80,000 to the contract with Anthonio, Inc., raising the limit from $1,185,050 to $1,265,050. It pays for five more months of full-time Inspector of Record services to commission and close out the project, as the Division of the State Architect requires. The term is extended to May 29, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $43,480.29 to G & G Builders' Peralta Elementary play matting project
output.summary: This change order adds up to $43,480.29 to the contract with G & G Builders, raising the limit from $160,946 to $204,426.29. The added work covers sawcutting and demolishing asphalt, pouring a concrete slab and patching asphalt for the play matting project at Peralta Elementary School.

output.headline: Pays Applied Materials & Engineering up to $11,701 for turf field testing at Westlake Middle
output.summary: The district is hiring Applied Materials & Engineering, Inc. to provide the construction inspection and testing that the Division of the State Architect requires for the new turf field at Westlake Middle School. The work runs from August 15, 2019 to no later than June 30, 2020, for no more than $11,701.

output.headline: Pays General Roofing up to $11,990 for temporary roof repairs at Foster Educational Leadership Complex
output.summary: The district is hiring General Roofing Company to make temporary roof repairs to two stair towers at the Foster Educational Leadership Complex, including cleaning off failing materials and reconfiguring roof drainage. The work was scheduled to begin July 1, 2019, before this approval, and finish by September 30, 2019, for no more than $11,990.

output.headline: Pays Anthonio up to $29,040 for turf field inspection at Claremont Middle School
output.summary: The district is hiring Anthonio, Inc. to provide the Inspector of Record services the Division of the State Architect requires for the new turf field at Claremont Middle School. The firm will also review construction documents, prepare reports and attend project meetings. The work runs from August 15, 2019 to no later than April 3, 2020, for no more than $29,040.

output.headline: Adds $156,397.94 to Redgwick's Claremont Middle School turf field contract
output.summary: This change order adds $156,397.94 to the district's contract with Redgwick Construction, raising the limit from $635,957.95 to $792,355.89. The added work is demolition and installation of a new turf at Claremont Middle School.

output.summary: The Board is approving the 2019-20 School Plan for Student Achievement (SPSA) for Bella Vista Elementary School, the school's annual plan for how it will serve students. No dollar amount is stated in the item.

output.headline: Adds $71,000 to Ninyo & Moore's LaEscuelita Educational Center work and extends it to Dec. 2019
output.summary: This amendment adds $71,000 to the contract with Ninyo & Moore, raising the limit from $65,000 to $136,000. The added services were requested by the California Department of Toxic Substances Control and include inspecting the accessible parts of the sub-slab ventilation system at the LaEscuelita Educational Center. The term is extended to December 31, 2019.

output.headline: Adds $145,340 for window water testing at Glenview and extends Applied Materials' contract to 2020
output.summary: This amendment adds $145,340 to the contract with Applied Materials & Engineering, Inc., raising the limit from $297,937 to $443,277. The added work is water testing of 214 windows and written reports for the Glenview new construction project. The term is extended to December 1, 2020.

output.headline: Approves a retirement-system exemption request for a recently retired teacher
output.summary: The Board approves Resolution No. 1920-0071, which asks for an exemption to the separation-from-service requirement of the California State Teachers Retirement System (CalSTRS) for a teacher who recently retired from the district. The item states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves a retirement-system exemption request for a retiring Health Services Coordinator
output.summary: The Board approves Resolution No. 1920-0072, which asks for an exemption to the separation-from-service requirement of the California State Teachers Retirement System (CalSTRS) for a Health Services Coordinator who is retiring from the district. The item states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Updates the Board policy on who may sign contracts, with two possible spending limits
output.summary: The Board is asked to amend Board Policy 3312 on contracts and delegation of authority. If approved, the policy would name which district positions can sign contracts up to the Consumer Price Index-adjusted limit in the Public Contract Code (currently $92,600), or which positions can sign contracts up to $50,000 per fiscal year in total with one vendor. The item involves no new spending.

output.headline: Accepts a $70,000 grant for substitute coverage so staff can attend new-teacher training
output.summary: The district is accepting a $70,000 grant from the Chiling Hammer Education Fund, through the East Bay Community Foundation. The money is for substitute coverage or extended contract time so staff can attend New Teachers Center professional development during the 2019-20 school year.

output.headline: Adopts Personnel Report No. 1920-0001
output.summary: The Board is adopting the first personnel report of the 2019-20 year, Personnel Report No. 1920-0001. The item text does not list the individual personnel actions or any dollar amounts.

output.headline: Creates or revises the job description for Truck Driver
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that approves a new or revised job description for the Truck Driver position. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies the Board President's appointment to the school facilities bond oversight committee
output.summary: The Board ratifies the Board President's appointment of a new member to the Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee for Measures A, B and J. The appointment takes effect August 15, 2019, and fills the unexpired term ending June 10, 2020.

output.headline: Reduces classified layoffs and adds classified positions for 2019-20 based on program need
output.summary: The Board is amending an earlier resolution so that fewer classified (non-teaching) positions are laid off and more classified positions are authorized for the 2019-20 fiscal year, based on program need. No dollar amount is stated.
